tests_added: examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 1: carriersOf lists a lens's carriers in model order, and nothing without a lens
examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 2: stepCarrier starts at the first carrier and wraps both ways
examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 3: stepping from a non-carrier goes to the first carrier after it in model order
examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 4: whyLit names the systems whose carriers lit a part, and says a carrier carries
examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 5: stepLensRead refuses without a lens, and names the part it leaves open
examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 6: read_view at L2 says where the open part sits in the walk, or why it is lit
examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 7 (guard): lensRead and read_view at L0/L1 light exactly what the lens lights
examples/atlas/test/evidence.test.ts::case 8: with no lens, the mast and the pane render no stepper
deviations_from_card: All eight cases live in test/evidence.test.ts (case 8's source check included) rather than spread into tools.test.ts/shell.test.ts; Shell.tsx needed no change (Mast, Pane and AtlasTools already receive lens and levels). whyLit takes the systems the drawing draws a part with (systemsDrawnWith: the lanes node's systems under LANES_LEVELS, else the component's own system), because the record node is lit by sys-brain, a system its item component is not in - own-system-only would leave that case unexplained. Red-before was measured against a throwing stub of evidence.ts. Pane carrier/step buttons use a new .at-lens-go class, not .at-chip, so shell.test.ts's aria-pressed check on the lens-toggle chip still finds the toggle. ADR 0176 added.
notes: Root `pnpm test` not run: it recurses into examples/journey (e2e, forbidden by the brief) and no workspace package imports atlas; the atlas suite (140 tests) is green. No sibling reds seen. Mast stepper/pane use colour-only hover transitions, no motion added.
